name: Return Address
invitation: Play catch across the launch deck. Send a ball down the clearing and bring it home to the other half of the deck. Start your reply from where it landed.
physicalQuestion: Can the end of one flight choose the starting place for another? Can a player trade sides, then steer a reply back to the first sender?
nearbySensitivity: From the serve, one yaw step from 4 to 4.5 degrees moves the tee landing from x +3.99 to +3.52 m. At the opening aim, every integer power setting from 62 through 81 percent returns via both faces to a reachable spot on the opposite half of the deck. The opening at 58 percent falls short. Moving the east face 0.5 m right gives a serve landing at x +4.52 m. Turning it by one 5-degree step shifts the landing by roughly 2.3 m.
validationEvidence: The Foundry checker replays eight terminals with the existing Havok range runner. The offline check also reads the body ledger, fires replies from the visible tee-contact x rounded to a carriage step, sweeps 1,225 local starting setups, and tests one-wall and empty controls. The short lob touches the opposite deck without a wall. A separately aimed flat bank can sustain a rally too. No owner or fresh-player trial.

limitations.concept: Verify that a return actually travelled down the yard.
limitations.missing: The manifest checker can replay the terminal and the none outcome, but cannot assert which bodies the ball touched in order. A short lob can also end on the opposite deck.
limitations.extension: Allow an optional ordered list of expected body IDs on a tested shot, checked against the existing contact record.

limitations.concept: Use the landing as the address for the next serve.
limitations.missing: The contact x is inside the expanded Contact record. A free-launch world with no goal inherits the Musical Workshop panel and its unrelated instructions.
limitations.extension: Reuse the Foundry invitation in that panel. For this handoff, show the contacted tee x and nearest carriage stop together in the receipt.
